canonical_question: How do the mechanical properties of the CuMoTaWV film translate to service conditions at elevated temperatures, given that 'sluggish diffusion' is temperature-dependent?

question_variants.question: How do the mechanical properties of the CuMoTaWV film translate to service conditions at elevated temperatures, given that 'sluggish diffusion' is temperature-dependent?
question_variants.resolution_summary: The paper mentions 'sluggish diffusion' contributes to high hardness and Young's modulus at room temperature. It discusses tribological behavior at room temperature and 300°C, noting a tribochemical reaction at 300°C. It does not provide data on how 'sluggish diffusion' or mechanical properties translate to elevated temperature service conditions or how the diffusion mechanism changes with temperature.

answers.answer: The paper states 'sluggish diffusion' contributes to measured high hardness and Young's modulus (measured at RT). At elevated temperatures (300°C), the paper observes high coefficient of friction due to tribochemical reactions, but does not explicitly link this to the temperature dependence of sluggish diffusion or predict property changes at higher service temperatures.
answers.measurement_outcome: high COF at 300°C due to tribochemical reaction
answers.mechanism: sluggish diffusion contributes to hardness/modulus (RT only)
answers.boundary_limitation: No data on mechanical properties or diffusion mechanism at temperatures beyond 300°C or specific service conditions.
evidence_spans: In this work, a refractory high-entropy alloy (RHEA) film of equimolar CuMoTaWV was deposited on silicon and 304 stainless-steel substrates using DC-magnetron sputtering.
A sputtering target was developed by partial sintering of an equimolar powder mixture of Cu, Mo, Ta, W, and V using spark plasma sintering.
The target was used to sputter a nanocrystalline RHEA film with a thickness of ∼900 nm and an average grain size of 18 nm.

source_evidence_spans: Furthermore, the high entropic effect, sluggish diffusion, and lattice distortion in RHEA films contribute to the measured high hardness and Young’s modulus.
